page: Amazon Web Services r8gd.4xlarge is a memory-optimized server instance powered by the AWS Graviton processor family. It features 16 dedicated physical cores based on the 64-bit ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 architecture, operating at a clock speed of 2.8 GHz. The processor configuration includes 64 KB of L1d cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 36 MB of L3 cache. The instance is equipped with 128.0 GB of system memory, providing a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per core.

This instance runs on the AWS Nitro hypervisor and includes 950 GB of local NVMe SSD instance storage. It provides a baseline network bandwidth of 8 Gbps. The inclusion of local NVMe SSDs makes it suitable for applications requiring low-latency scratch space or high-speed local caching. No dedicated GPU hardware is included in this configuration.

In benchmark testing, the r8gd.4xlarge demonstrates strong memory performance, achieving a top-tier rating in the Passmark memory score and a strong rating for large-block uncached memory read and write bandwidth. Database operations also score in the top 25%. However, CPU-bound tasks like stress-ng and Geekbench single-core and multi-core tests fall into the average category. The instance exhibits poor performance in large language model inference tasks, particularly for text generation, making it less suitable for AI workloads.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ARM64 architecture combined with high memory density and integrated NVMe storage offers a balanced profile for memory-intensive workloads without the premium of x86 hardware. The server is highly suited for database operations, caching layers like Redis, memory-intensive data processing, and applications requiring high memory bandwidth alongside fast local storage.
